subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord plugin-owned bot self-profile mutation surface, and should it reuse the existing set-profile action pattern or introduce a Discord-only self-profile/selfProfile contract?
rationale: This creates a public config/action surface that mutates Discord bot identity through stored credentials, so automation should not choose the authorization, account-routing, validation, audit, naming, and partial-failure contract alone.

options.title: Approve narrow self-profile surface
options.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off, self-only profile mutation action with explicit account selection, avatar validation, regression tests, docs, and live Discord proof, preferably reusing set-profile unless maintainers want a Discord-specific name.

options.title: Keep presence-only scope
options.body: Leave nickname/avatar mutation out of OpenClaw for now and route only status/activity needs through the existing presence action or the open dynamic-presence API discussion.

options.title: Defer identity mutation model
options.body: Wait to design a broader identity model across self-profile, per-binding identity, and webhook/persona delivery before adding any Discord bot profile mutation path.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-profile surface
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off, self-only profile mutation action with explicit account selection, avatar validation, regression tests, docs, and live Discord proof, preferably reusing set-profile unless maintainers want a Discord-specific name.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord presence work and the merged PR explicitly left self-profile as a separate scope.
